features.title: Data directory
features.behavior: kb init creates the data directory, seeds the sample documents, and records every seeded document in the metadata index.

features.title: Document list
features.behavior: kb list reports every known document with id, title, filename, line count, and origin, from the metadata index alone.

features.title: Question answering
features.behavior: kb ask answers a question with at most two cited lines, or says nothing matched; the citation contract is unchanged from project 01.
features.verification: kb ask --data-dir kb-data "Which lines become citations in the ranking?"

features.title: App starts
features.behavior: kb serve --self-check binds the loopback HTTP server, answers /health, /documents, and the first document's /documents/{id}, and shuts down cleanly.

features.title: Document import
features.behavior: kb import copies a new file into the data directory and records it in the metadata index with origin imported.

features.title: Document detail
features.behavior: kb show returns the imported document's metadata entry plus its full content.

evidence.observed:
exit 0: {"id":"field-guide","title":"Field guide to importing","filename":"field-guide.md","lines":20,"origin":"imported","content":"# Field guide to importing

Importing is the moment a document becomes part of the knowledge base
instead of a file that happens to sit nearby. The import command copies
the file into the documents folder and, just as important, records it in
the metadata index.

## Why the metadata index exists

A directory scan tells you what files exist; the metadata index tells you
what the system knows. Listing reads the index, never the directory, so
the answer to "what is in the knowledge base" comes from recorded state
rather than rediscovery. That is the system of record principle applied
to a single JSON file.

## What survives a restart

Everything: the copied document, its index entry, its title and line
count. A fresh process lists the imported document without re-reading the
original source, which is the whole point of persistence.
"}

features.title: Metadata persistence
features.behavior: A fresh process lists the imported document from index/documents-meta.json alone; nothing depends on process memory.
